column8: Registered tests execute the canonical Datum state and direct fold seam across current scalar families, NULL/unseen distinction, merge, reset, representable source spill layouts, and representable memory behavior. No Database query reaches FIRSTROW through the current parser, every group expression is eagerly resolved before folding, and Go typed harness breadth plus unrepresented value families remain open.

First physical row, later state-update short circuit, first-row NULL, independent flags/payload, source/destination merge precedence, empty source state, and all current Datum payload families use one canonical state. Float32 identity, temporal, duration, JSON, enum, set, vector, typed Eval/chunk output, parser reachability, and short-circuiting expression evaluation remain open.

Rust asserts the exact first-retained String payload charge and zero charge for ignored rows. Go's ten type-specific unsafe.Sizeof allocation values, JSON/enum/set payload deltas, and executor memory tracking remain open.

Independent source flags and Decimal runtime values exist, but Rust does not yet reproduce Go MyDecimal's raw in-memory spill encoding, including hidden precision and word layout; the former Rust-only decimal codec was removed rather than counted as parity.
The exact -123, 0, and 123 payloads and all three source flag combinations round-trip through two bool bytes followed by native-endian int64, matching Go SerializeInt64 with no extra tag.
Independent source spill flags are implemented, but Datum has no MySQL Time variant or source-compatible Time payload yet.

The empty string and exact source long-string seed doubled ten times round-trip through two bool bytes, native-width length, and raw payload; tests also prove collation is external metadata and reusable capacity grows.
Datum currently exposes only f64 Real, so encoding these values as Real would erase the source Float32 type identity; no false coverage is claimed.
The exact -1.1, 0, and 1.1 payloads and all three source flag combinations round-trip through two bool bytes followed by native IEEE-754 f64 bytes, matching Go SerializeFloat64 with no extra tag.
Independent source spill flags are implemented, but Datum has no MySQL Duration-plus-FSP variant yet.
Independent source spill flags and variable-width buffer reuse are implemented, but Datum has no BinaryJSON type-code/payload variant yet.
Independent source spill flags and string payload mechanics are implemented, but Datum cannot retain Enum name and numeric identity as one typed value yet.
Independent source spill flags and string payload mechanics are implemented, but Datum cannot retain Set name and numeric identity as one typed value yet.
